name: Inclusion
definition: You recognize your biases and work to counteract them; you work to ensure everyone at Netflix can do their best work, whatever their culture, identity or background.

rows.under: Gives it to the person who already looks like the last person who had it.
rows.justRight: Notices the pattern, and gives the work to the person who is ready, including when they are not the familiar choice.
rows.over: Assigns the stretch to make a point about the pattern, and the person is not set up to succeed.

rows.situation: A meeting where the same people always speak
rows.under: Lets the pattern stand and calls it merit.
rows.justRight: Asks the people who have not spoken, and weighs what they say by the work, not by how familiar it sounds.
rows.over: Polices airtime so tightly that the people with the facts cannot finish a thought.

rows.situation: A team habit that only works for one kind of schedule or background
rows.under: Treats the habit as neutral and tells people to adapt.
rows.justRight: Changes the habit when it keeps someone from doing their best work, and keeps the part that the work actually needs.
rows.over: Drops every shared norm, including the ones that make the work coherent.

rows.situation: Your first read on a person you do not know well
rows.under: Trusts the first read and builds the next decision on it.
rows.justRight: Names the bias you are likely to have, checks it against the work, and changes the read when the work disagrees.
rows.over: Refuses to form any judgment about performance, because every judgment might be bias.

rows.situation: A program, event, or slogan about belonging
rows.under: Counts the program as the result.
rows.justRight: Judges it by whether people can do their best work here, and stops the parts that are only a slogan.
rows.over: Uses today's output as a reason to dismiss a change that would let more people do their best work.
